title: Cross-peer failure-chain and route-boundary reconciliation
mode: Primary-source issue/repository review plus local source/plan audit
head: de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
scope: Refresh current open-source DWG/DXF route declarations and peer issue/PR status
Separate page/container decode, object-map/owner traversal, serialization, publication, and downstream consumer failures
Reconcile peer failure shapes with current local parser, graph, output-transaction, and PAR-139 owners
Refine implementation and evidence readiness without adding duplicate findings or validation burden

sources.name: LibreDWG AC1021 page decoding and object-map/output failures
sources.observed: PR #1363 merged on 2026-08-07 and closed #1361 after tracing near-DBL_MAX AC1021 LWPOLYLINE values to Reed-Solomon-coded incompressible pages being treated as verbatim. PR #1360 remains open and proposes narrowly resynchronizing after a malformed modular character; its author corrected the original section-size theory. PR #1359 remains open and proposes skipping unresolved owned-entity references. Issue #1355 separately states that a writer stopping before required sections/terminal EOF must not report complete success. These are distinct failure layers and peer behaviors, not local defects.

sources.name: LibreDWG root dictionary ordering report and Autodesk OBJECTS contract
sources.observed: The still-open peer report describes a lower-handle extension dictionary being selected before the true NOD in two drawings from a private 43-file corpus. The Autodesk DXF OBJECTS rule identifies the NOD positionally as the first object; handle order is not the identity rule. The report supports the existing non-monotonic-handle/root-role control and does not require a new finding.

sources.name: ACadSharp current issue families
sources.observed: The selected reports span codepage label/payload mismatch, a versioned GeoData tail, legacy compound-record interpretation, locale-sensitive lookup, recursive-work exhaustion, and whole-file native writer rejection. They belong to separate parser, writer, locale, resource-bound, and composed-consumer questions; no single issue or aggregate version matrix can settle them.

sources.name: DXF-only/projection comparators and downstream consumer route
sources.observed: ezdxf documents strict parsing separately from recovery/audit; IxMilia documents entity/version and AutoCAD-writer caveats; GDAL's DXF driver is an OGR projection with Binary DXF input from GDAL 3.12, while its DWG driver is separately ODA-dependent; FreeCAD #31835 concerns converter fallback/false-success orchestration rather than the libdxfrw codec.

localEvidence: DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md PAR-14/PAR-49/7BE/7F.1 already separates page decoding, object-map bounds, owner graph disposition, strict output completion, and atomic publication
Local dwgReader21::parseDataPage and dwgReader18::parseDataPage perform the applicable page decoding before entity parse; no page-valid local LWPOLYLINE failure was demonstrated in this research pass
Local DXF writer preserves/regenerates NOD first and has generated non-monotonic-handle graph controls
Existing codepage, GeoData, legacy VERTEX, bounded-progress, and composed FreeCAD owners cover the selected ACadSharp/FreeCAD failure shapes
PAR-139 remains the only new local feature finding in this review horizon; PAR-139.1 remains the first codec hardening slice

assessment.planImpact: Reinforces the existing layered failure model and exact route evidence requirements. Keep strict-complete conversion fail-closed and atomic; any future tolerant skip/recovery mode must record exact source identities and losses and remain non-promoting. Continue PAR-139.1 locally before adapter/graph/composed checks; peer and platform runs remain at their existing composed checkpoints.

method.kind: Read-only primary-source web review and local source/plan inspection
method.limitations: Peer issue reports, release notes, and mutable repository pages are source evidence, not independent reproductions or normative DWG/DXF layouts. PR #1363's merge and issue closure establish the peer's reported fix path only; open PR proposals #1360 and #1359 are not current release behavior. The existing PAR-139 code changes in the shared worktree were not built or tested by this research pass.
